1.

Learned A.G.A. informs that he has procured complete instructions in the matter including up-to-date case diary and the opposite party no.2 (complainant) of this case has also been served at their end.

In this regard, a communication sent by the S.H.O. of concerned Police Station Ramgaon,
District Bahraich of date 03.01.2023 has been placed before this Court for perusal and the same has been taken on record.
Thus, it is reflected that despite being served, the opposite party no.2 (complainant) is not represented before this Court.

2. Heard Shri Manoj Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the accused-applicant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3.

This bail application has been moved by the accused/applicant- Amit Kumar for grant of bail, in Case Crime No. 420 of 2023, under Sections 457, 354, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C. and Section 7/8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, Police Station Ramgaon, District Bahraich, during trial.

4. Learned counsel for the accused-applicant while pressing the bail application submits that it is a case of false implication.

The first information report of this case has been lodged by the uncle of the prosecutrix/victim on 21.09.2023 alleging that the applicant had entered into his house and molested his niece and when an alarm was raised, his father and brother has also arrived and started assaulting the informant and with their help the applicant fled away from the scene.
5. It is vehemently submitted that the instant F.I.R. is nothing but the result of established enmity between the families on the basis of a dispute pertaining to 'nali'(drainage).

6. It is further submitted that in the F.I.R. which is apparently lodged by an alleged eye witness and in the statement of the informant as well as of victim recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., there was no whisper with regard to the commission of rape.
However, when the statement of the prosecutrix was recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., she for the first time alleged commission of rape also.

However, the investigating officer after thoroughly investigating the incident has not been found the allegations of commission of rape truthful and the charge sheet could only be filed under Section 354 I.P.C. along with other relevant penal sections.
7.

It is next submitted that the victim also refused to undergo any medical examination on 21.09.2023 and in this regard the attention of this Court has been drawn towards Annexure No.-3,
which is a memo pertaining to the medical examination of the prosecutrix whereon her refusal to undergo internal or regular medical examination has been endorsed.
8.

It is vehemently submitted that after many days of the alleged incident, the prosecutrix appears to have been medically examined i.e. on 30.09.2023, however, her medical report are clean and no injury of any kind or any pathological abnormality has been noticed therein.

9. While drawing the attention of this Court towards the statement of many independent witnesses i.e. Kamlesh Kumar, Rakesh, etc., it is submitted that these witnesses have stated that the victim has stated in the village that she has falsely implicated the applicant and his family members.

10. It is also submitted that statement of many other witnesses have been recorded by the investigating officer, who have deposed in favour of the informant and even if their statement is taken on their face, the offence may not travel beyond Section 354 I.P.C.
11.

It is further submitted that the age of the prosecutrix is shown as 14 years, 06 months and 05 days on the basis of educational credentials but the same may not be deemed or taken conclusive as the same is yet to be finally adjudicated by the trial court.
Applicant is languishing in jail in this case since 14.10.2023.
Charge sheet in this case has already been filed and there is no apprehension that after being released on bail he may flee from the course of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.

12. Learned A.G.A. on the other hand submits that incident of outraging the modesty and molestation has been committed with a girl of very tender age and, therefore, applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.

sentences.text: 13. Perusal of the record would reveal that the F.I.R. of the case has been lodged by the uncle of the victim.

Admittedly, initially the prosecutrix refused to undergo any medical examination, however,
after many days of the incident she was subjected to medical examination and no abnormality or injury of any kind has been found on her person.

During the course of alleged scuffle, the informant is shown to have sustained only one visible injury i.e. of the nature of scratch and the defence of the applicant appears to be that the same on the basis of alleged enmity may be self-manufactured.
The allegations in the F.I.R., in the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. as well as of the informant are with regard to the molestation only.

However, an improvement appears to have been made by the prosecutrix in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. with regard to the commission of rape, which has not been found truthful during the course of investigation, as the charge sheet has not been submitted under Section 376 I.P.C.
Applicant is languishing in jail in this case since 14.10.2023 without any criminal antecedents.
Charge sheet in this case has also been filed and the presence of the applicant may be secured before the trial court by placing adequate conditions.

14. Keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the considered view that applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is thus allowed.

15. Let the accused/applicant- Amit Kumar involved in above-mentioned case, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
(ii) The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
16. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
17. Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the Court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
18. Observations made herein-above by this court are only for the purpose of disposal of this bail application and shall not be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.
